theorems.name: von Neumann-Morgenstern Axioms for Expected Utility
theorems.description: Expected utility over finite-outcome lotteries is affine in the lottery mixture; the induced preference satisfies independence and Archimedean continuity (an indifference weight α ∈ (0,1) exists); and, for normalized lotteries, the preference is invariant under positive affine rescaling of the utility. Completeness and transitivity of the preference are proved in the source module (prefersEU_total, prefersEU_trans) but are not restated in this entry. Soundness direction only: the vNM representation theorem (axioms imply an expected-utility form) is not delivered.

import MathFin.RiskMeasures.VonNeumannMorgenstern

open MathFin

/-- The pivot of the vNM development: expected utility is affine in the lottery mixture,
    `EU(αp + (1−α)q) = α·EU(p) + (1−α)·EU(q)`. Needs no hypotheses on the lotteries —
    it is linearity of the finite sum, and it is exactly what fails for the non-linear
    functionals invented to explain the Allais paradox. -/
theorem vnm_expected_utility_mix
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (u : ι → ℝ) (α : ℝ) (p q : ι → ℝ) :
    MathFin.expectedUtility s u (MathFin.mix α p q)
      = α * MathFin.expectedUtility s u p + (1 - α) * MathFin.expectedUtility s u q :=
  MathFin.expectedUtility_mix s u α p q

/-- vNM independence: mixing a common lottery into both sides preserves the
    expected-utility preference, at any nonnegative weight. -/
theorem vnm_independence
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (u : ι → ℝ) {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α)
    {p q r : ι → ℝ} (h : MathFin.prefersEU s u p q) :
    MathFin.prefersEU s u (MathFin.mix α p r) (MathFin.mix α q r) :=
  MathFin.prefersEU_independence s u hα h

/-- vNM continuity (the Archimedean axiom): strictly between a better and a worse lottery,
    some strict mixture of the outer pair is exactly indifferent to the middle one; the
    weight is exhibited as the position of the middle utility on the outer utility
    interval, not obtained from a limit. -/
theorem vnm_continuity
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (u : ι → ℝ) {p q r : ι → ℝ}
    (hpq : MathFin.expectedUtility s u q < MathFin.expectedUtility s u p)
    (hqr : MathFin.expectedUtility s u r < MathFin.expectedUtility s u q) :
    ∃ α : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ α < 1 ∧
      MathFin.expectedUtility s u (MathFin.mix α p r) = MathFin.expectedUtility s u q :=
  MathFin.prefersEU_continuity s u hpq hqr

/-- vNM cardinality: a positive affine rescaling of the utility induces exactly the same
    preference on lotteries — utility is cardinal only up to origin and scale. -/
theorem vnm_affine_invariance
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (u : ι → ℝ) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    {p q : ι → ℝ} (hp : ∑ i ∈ s, p i = 1) (hq : ∑ i ∈ s, q i = 1) :
    MathFin.prefersEU s (fun i ↦ a * u i + b) p q ↔ MathFin.prefersEU s u p q :=
  MathFin.prefersEU_affine_invariant s u ha hp hq

theorems.description: For α ∈ (0, 1) and every probability law μ on ℝ with finite second moment, each expected asymmetric squared loss ∫ α((y − e)⁺)² + (1 − α)((e − y)⁺)² dμ(y) is finite, and the α-expectile of μ (the root e of α E[(Y − e)⁺] = (1 − α) E[(e − Y)⁺]) is its unique minimizer over forecasts e ∈ ℝ. Also, for an integrable Y the 1/2-expectile is the mean E[Y].

theorems.name: Gaussian VaR and ES Are Standard-Deviation Premium Principles
theorems.description: For a loss X with law N(m, v) and α ∈ (0, 1): VaR_α(X) = E[X] + Φ⁻¹(α)·sd(X), the standard-deviation principle with loading Φ⁻¹(α); and if v ≠ 0, ES_α(X) = E[X] + (ϕ(Φ⁻¹(α))/(1 − α))·sd(X), the principle with loading ϕ(Φ⁻¹(α))/(1 − α), where ϕ is the standard normal density. VaR and ES are the library's general (quantile-based) definitions.

theorems.name: Expected-Utility Acceptance Sets Are Convex but Need Not Be Coherent
theorems.description: On a finite state space with weights p ≥ 0, a position X is acceptable to an expected-utility agent with utility u and wealth W if u(W) ≤ Σ p_i u(W + X_i). For concave u, every convex combination of two acceptable positions is acceptable. A binary Kelly bet of fraction f at odds b (win probability p) is acceptable under log utility at unit wealth iff its expected log-growth p log(1 + fb) + (1 − p) log(1 − f) is nonnegative. On a fair coin at unit wealth, log utility accepts X = (1/2, −1/4) but rejects 3X, so no coherent risk measure of losses (Artzner–Delbaen–Eber–Heath axioms in the loss convention, for any finite measure on the two states) has the log-utility acceptance set {L : ρ(L) ≤ 0}, where a loss L is acceptable when the position −L is (log is Mathlib's Real.log, equal to log|x| at nonpositive wealth). Only this explicit counterexample is proved, not a general statement about all strictly concave utilities.

import MathFin.RiskMeasures.UtilityDerivation

    (hu : ∀ x y : ℝ, ∀ α : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ 1 →
      α * u x + (1 - α) * u y ≤ u (α * x + (1 - α) * y))

    (hX : acceptableUnderUtility s p u W X) (hY : acceptableUnderUtility s p u W Y) :
    acceptableUnderUtility s p u W (fun i ↦ α * X i + (1 - α) * Y i) :=
  acceptableUnderUtility_convex s p u W hp hu hα hα1 hX hY

nonnegative. -/

    acceptableUnderUtility Finset.univ ![p, 1 - p] Real.log 1 ![f * b, -f] ↔
      0 ≤ kellyGrowth p b f :=
  acceptableUnderUtility_log_iff_kellyGrowth p b f

theorems.name: Euler Allocation of Gaussian Portfolio VaR
theorems.description: For a Gaussian vector X of risk-factor changes, weights w with positive portfolio variance wᵀΣw (Σ the covariance kernel of X) and α ∈ (0, 1): the value-at-risk of the portfolio loss Σ wᵢXᵢ is its mean Σ wᵢ E Xᵢ plus the parametric VaR Φ⁻¹(α)√(wᵀΣw), and the component VaRs wᵢ Φ⁻¹(α)(Σw)ᵢ/√(wᵀΣw) sum to VaR_α(Σ wᵢXᵢ) − Σ wᵢ E Xᵢ. For any symmetric kernel with positive portfolio variance, the marginal VaRs α(Σx)ᵢ/√(xᵀΣx) are the partial derivatives of x ↦ α√(xᵀΣx): its derivative along any direction d is Σ dᵢ · marginalVaRᵢ.

import MathFin.RiskMeasures.ComponentVaR

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open MathFin

/-- The VaR of a Gaussian portfolio loss is its mean plus the parametric VaR at `Φ⁻¹(α)`. -/
theorem gaussian_var_eq_portfolioVaRN_thm {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {Ω : Type*}
    {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → ℝ} {α : ℝ}
    (hX : HasGaussianLaw (fun ω ↦ (X · ω)) P) (w : ι → ℝ) (hα : α ∈ Ioo 0 1) :
    valueAtRisk (fun ω ↦ ∑ i, w i * X i ω) P α =
      ∑ i, w i * P[X i] +
        portfolioVaRN Finset.univ w (fun i j ↦ cov[X i, X j; P]) (PhiInv α) :=
  valueAtRisk_portfolio_gaussian_eq_portfolioVaRN hX w hα

/-- The component VaRs allocate the Gaussian portfolio VaR in excess of the mean. -/
theorem component_var_gaussian_euler_thm {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {Ω : Type*}
    {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → ℝ} {α : ℝ}
    (hX : HasGaussianLaw (fun ω ↦ (X · ω)) P) (w : ι → ℝ) (hα : α ∈ Ioo 0 1)
    (hvar : 0 < portfolioVarN Finset.univ w fun i j ↦ cov[X i, X j; P]) :
    ∑ i, componentVaR Finset.univ w (fun i j ↦ cov[X i, X j; P]) (PhiInv α) i =
      valueAtRisk (fun ω ↦ ∑ i, w i * X i ω) P α - ∑ i, w i * P[X i] :=
  sum_componentVaR_eq_valueAtRisk_sub hX w hα hvar

theorems.name: SA-CCR Effective Notional as a Standard Deviation
theorems.description: Let D₀, D₁, D₂ be the signed effective notionals of the three maturity buckets of an SA-CCR interest-rate hedging set.
